existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: `DeviceMetric` has multiple local breaking changes despite stable resource identity. Top concerns are mandatory `status`, mandatory `device` replacing R4 device-link fields, and primitive-code-to-CodeableConcept conversions with terminology changes. The main uncertainty is not whether the computable changes exist, but the intended migration policy for ambiguous mappings.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should be treated as a transform, not a version relabel. R4 `category`, `color`, and calibration codes need to be wrapped as CodeableConcepts with appropriate coding systems; `measurementPeriod` must be reinterpreted as a Quantity frequency where possible; `source`/`parent` references need policy-driven consolidation into `device`; and all migrated resources need a new lifecycle `status`.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for element presence, cardinality, type, binding, flag, and local terminology changes because they are directly visible in the R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions and local CodeSystems. Confidence is medium for migration impact details where the local inputs lack official change notes, narrative migration guidance, and ConceptMaps for several replacements.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
DeviceMetric keeps its resource identity. The aggregate has 7 hard R4-to-R6 instance break(s), 0 potential hard break(s), 1 non-mechanical migration finding(s), and 0 direct behavior/API finding(s).

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 1, which creates weak stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 52/100, producing migration shape `moderate-targeted-remodel`, major migration `Partial`, and compatibility posture `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`.

11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Expect targeted migration work, but continue reviewing individual breaks. Use less-breaking designs where they do not preserve obsolete or conflicting models indefinitely.

topFindings.title: R4 `source` and `parent` references are removed and replaced by mandatory `device`
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus R6-to-R4 loss: old reference names are invalid in R6, missing the new required reference is invalid, and a single R6 device reference does not always map back cleanly to R4 source versus parent.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: R6 adds mandatory modifier `DeviceMetric.status` with no R4 element
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus runtime/API/codegen and R6-to-R4 loss: R4 instances lack the required field, R6 consumers must inspect the modifier, and R6 lifecycle values have no base R4 slot.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: `category` changes from required primitive code to extensible CodeableConcept
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus runtime/API/codegen: a primitive string representation is invalid where R6 expects CodeableConcept, and generated client/server types change.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: `measurementPeriod` Timing is removed and replaced by `measurementFrequency` Quantity
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and possible R6-to-R4 loss: the old element name/type is gone, and Timing schedules and Quantity frequencies are not fully equivalent in either direction.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: `color` changes from R4 metric-color code to R6 CodeableConcept bound to color-codes
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus R6-to-R4 loss: the primitive R4 code shape is invalid in R6 and expanded R6 colors or RGB values cannot always be represented in R4.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and R6-to-R4 loss: the old entered-in-error code is no longer valid for operationalStatus, and R6 unknown has no exact R4 required-bound code.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.
